title: Basel Committee meets to advance supervisory and regulatory initiatives and discuss risks and vulnerabilities to the global banking system
key_claim: The Basel Committee met in Indonesia on 28-29 September 2026, is reviewing targeted elements of its prudential standard for banks' exposures to cryptoassets, and expects to provide an update by the end of the year.
frame_summary: Reports that the global bank capital standard for cryptoassets is still under targeted review, with an update promised by the end of 2026 and no content yet.
verbatim_quote: The Committee advanced its review and expects to provide an update by the end of the year.
verbatim_list: The Committee is reviewing targeted elements of its prudential standard for banks' exposures to cryptoassets.

title: EBA response to the European Commission's targeted consultation on the review of MiCA
key_claim: Under Article 501d CRR an EU bank's exposure to a tokenised traditional asset is treated as an exposure to the asset the token represents, anticipating full implementation of Basel SCO 60; the EBA says the absence of a fully harmonised EU definition of 'financial instrument' can only be remedied by legislative action and that treatment of trading book, hedging and netting is unclear if tokenised instruments stop being financial instruments.
frame_summary: Argues that parity for tokenised assets in EU bank capital rests on a financial-instrument definition that EU law has not harmonised and only legislation can fix.
verbatim_quote: can only be remedied by legislative action.
verbatim_list: it is unclear how those exposures should be treated by credit institutions, in particular for
trading book positions and for hedging and netting purposes.
including for the purposes of the credit risk and market risk framework (Article 501d CRR).

title: Implementing the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act for the Issuance of Stablecoins by Entities Subject to the Jurisdiction of the OCC (final rule)
key_claim: The OCC final rule implementing the GENIUS Act for stablecoin issuers is effective on 18 January 2027 and includes capital and operational backstop requirements; it concerns issuers and does not set bank capital for tokenised securities.
frame_summary: Reports that the US has finished a capital rule for payment stablecoin issuers, effective January 2027, while saying nothing on bank capital for tokenised securities.
verbatim_quote: The final rule is effective on January 18, 2027.

title: Prudential treatment of tokenised assets, stablecoins and other cryptoasset exposures (Dear CEO letter)
date_evidence: 18 May 2026 Dear Chief Executive Officer, In 2022, the Prudential Regulation Authority
key_claim: The PRA says tokenised traditional assets would in general receive the same prudential treatment as non-tokenised equivalents where the legal rights conferred are identical and the underlying risks comparable; the position is interim, a 100% capital requirement applies to unbacked cryptoassets, and the PRA expects to consult on a framework in 2028 at the earliest.
frame_summary: Sets out conditional capital parity for tokenised traditional assets as an interim UK supervisory position pending the Basel review and a PRA consultation no earlier than 2028.
verbatim_quote: expects to consult on a proposed framework in 2028 at the earliest
verbatim_list: tokenised traditional assets would, in general, receive the same prudential treatment as their non-tokenised equivalents
where the legal rights conferred are identical and the underlying risks are comparable.
These expectations will continue to be on an interim basis until the PRA publishes its proposed future prudential framework

title: New horizons: the legal and commercial frontier of digital assets (speech by Sasha Mills)
key_claim: The Bank of England's Executive Director for Financial Market Infrastructure says a tokenised security needs a legally authoritative record, ownership must be evidenced and transferred, competing claims must be resolvable, and a full roadmap will be published later this year.
frame_summary: Argues that the foundation for tokenised securities is legal: an authoritative record, evidenced ownership and resolvable competing claims, with a roadmap due before the end of 2026.
verbatim_quote: A tokenised security needs a legally authoritative record.
verbatim_list: Later this year, we will publish a full Roadmap which will provide a clear forward path,

title: What Is Needed for Tokenization to Deliver (IMF Blog, drawing on Chapter 3 of the October 2026 Global Financial Stability Report)
key_claim: Tokenized markets are growing rapidly but remain very small and fragmented; tokenised repo averages around $300 billion to $350 billion in daily volume against about $13 trillion daily in the US repo market; investors require legal certainty that tokenized assets represent enforceable rights; scaling can amplify risks.
frame_summary: Argues that tokenization can deliver only if legal certainty, regulatory clarity, interoperability and safe settlement money come first, because scaling a small, fragmented market amplifies risk.

title: The end of the beginning: digital assets enter the hard middle
key_claim: SCO60's implementation date was 1 January 2026 but jurisdictions are taking divergent approaches pending the review's outcome: Hong Kong has implemented, the EU partially, Canada with targeted changes, Singapore has delayed and the USA will not implement in the current form; the UK position is interim and a consultation is expected in 2028 at the earliest.
frame_summary: Argues that banks face divergent national treatments of the Basel crypto standard while the review runs, leaving a gap in prudential rules that needs urgent attention.
verbatim_quote: A consultation on a proposed UK framework is expected in 2028 at the earliest.
verbatim_list: some have delayed (eg Singapore), others (eg USA) will not implement in the current form.
